findings.evidence: The file already provides `permToBrauer_val_inl/inr`, `throughPerm_apply`, and `permToBrauerEquiv_apply/symm_apply`, so exposing all three bodies leaks implementation details unnecessarily.
findings.fix: Remove these `@[expose]` annotations and make the `rfl` API proofs elaborate without downstream unfolding, e.g. with `:= (rfl)` where needed.
findings.issue: `permToBrauer`, `throughPerm` (line 195), and `permToBrauerEquiv` (line 228) are `@[expose]` even though their behavior should be mediated by the adjacent application and inverse lemmas.

findings.evidence: The declaration defines `toFun` and `invFun` at lines 197–198, while the only public nearby lemmas are `restrict_extend` and `extend_restrict`; `rg` finds no `fiberEquiv_apply` or `fiberEquiv_symm_apply`.
findings.fix: Add `[simp]` lemmas identifying `fiberEquiv hab D` with `D.1.restrict D.2` and `(fiberEquiv hab).symm E` with `⟨extend hab E, extend_apply_left hab E⟩`.
findings.issue: `PerfectMatching.fiberEquiv` is opaque and has no forward or inverse application lemmas, so consumers cannot use its advertised restrict/extend correspondence without unfolding an unavailable body.

summary: Several public constructions expose implementation bodies despite having, or needing, characteristic lemmas. The advertised fiber equivalence also lacks usable forward and inverse application rules.
